_comment: Subjects the gateway operator LOOKED FOR and could not honestly publish. This file is
not a Sustainability Metadata Document and is not served as one: the leading underscore
keeps it out of the subject registry. Its entries appear in the index (HTML and
index.json) under 'publishes no machine-readable data', and a request for one of these
subjects' documents returns 404 - the draft's no-data rule - with the finding in the body.
This is deliberate. A registry that silently omits the organizations that publish nothing
would overstate how much of the web is measurable. The gap is the evidence.

subjects.finding: No Scope 1/2/3, energy, or renewable figures exist in any primary source. The FY2025 Form 10-K (filed February 2026) contains zero occurrences of climate, greenhouse, carbon, emission, scope or sustainab. The investor ESG environmental page is qualitative only ('a relatively light environmental footprint'). A 2022 blog post says the company was 'currently working to determine our carbon baseline'; no baseline has been published since. The widely-quoted 'PUE averaging 1.15' is a community-forum answer by a user, not a company statement, and is not used here.

GitHub publishes no standalone GHG inventory. Its only company-environmental blog post (2021-04-22) states commitments with no Scope 1/2/3 figures and links no inventory document. GitHub is a wholly owned Microsoft subsidiary and falls inside Microsoft's consolidated operational-control reporting boundary, so its emissions are reported within Microsoft Corporation's inventory. Deriving GitHub-specific figures by apportioning Microsoft's totals would be an invention and is not done.
